# launch_moonlight

[← Command index](README.md)

Start the Moonlight game-streaming client installed by setup_tools.

## Synopsis

```text
launch_moonlight [options]
```

## Description

Runs the Moonlight program from the tools directory. It streams the host's app
straight away: the host from `--host` or `[Tools.Moonlight] moonlight_host`
(192.168.1.12 by default), the app from `--app` or `[Tools.Moonlight] moonlight_app`
(Pegasus by default). With `moonlight_host` cleared it opens Moonlight's host list.

`--pair` pairs with the host instead: Moonlight shows a PIN, which is entered on the
host's Sunshine web page (port 47990). A host only has to be paired once.

It waits for Moonlight to exit and logs an error if it exits with a non-zero code.

## Options

### Stream

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--host <host>` | Sunshine host to stream from, by address or name; defaults to `[Tools.Moonlight] moonlight_host`. |
| `--app <app>` | App on the host to start; defaults to `[Tools.Moonlight] moonlight_app`. |
| `--pair` | Pair with the host instead of streaming. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Stream the configured host's app

```bash
launch_moonlight
```

### Pair with a host

```bash
launch_moonlight --host 192.168.1.20 --pair
```

### Stream Steam Big Picture from a host

```bash
launch_moonlight --host 192.168.1.20 --app "Steam Big Picture"
```

## Notes

- Moonlight must be installed first (`setup_tools -k Moonlight`); the command exits with an error if
  it is not found.
- Set `[Tools.Moonlight] moonlight_autostart` and install the bootstrap's `autostart` component to
  start it at every login.
